note: The study order of the 72 chapters, as chapter ids. Position in this list becomes the displayed 'Chapter N' and the Learn path order. Ids are stable, so reordering never disturbs saved progress (which is keyed by id in localStorage). Content difficulty must never descend: every chapter's `level` has to be >= the one before it. `why` records the dependency that pins each chapter here — keep it truthful, it is what the next editor reads before moving anything.

path.why: Hangul first — nothing is readable without it.
Greetings: the first thing you can actually say to someone.
N이에요/예요 + 은/는 — the first full sentence shape.
있어요/없어요 + 이/가 — needs the copula from ch3 to contrast against.
Present tense + 을/를 — the first action sentences.
에/에서 — places and times need a verb to attach to (ch5).
Food and shopping: first real errand, reuses 을/를 and 에서.
-고 싶어요, -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요 — first modal wants/abilities.
Requests and permission — the survival endings for a shop or a classroom.
Travel help: applies ch9 requests to getting around.
-아서/-고/-(으)면 — joins the A1 sentences into speech.
PAST TENSE. Nothing above A1 works without it; it was stranded at position 40.
Future/intention — the natural pair to past tense.
Question words: you cannot hold a conversation asking nothing.
Numbers and time — needed for prices, dates, and appointments.
Counters: requires the two number systems from the previous chapter.
Negation deep dive — 안/못/-지 않아요 gathered once the tenses exist.
Irregular conjugation: only meaningful once past tense shows the irregular stems.
Noun modifiers A-(으)ㄴ N / V-는 N — the first step beyond simple sentences.
Comparisons N보다 더 — needs the adjectives and modifiers from ch21.
Suggestions -(으)ㄹ까요?/-아 보다 — how you propose doing something together.
Directions and transport: (으)로 and -(으)러 가요 in a real errand.
Pronunciation rules — placed once there is enough material to hear them in.
-고 있다 ongoing action, the first aspect distinction.
-고 나서/-자마자 sequence — builds on the aspect idea.
-다가 mid-action change: needs ongoing (ch27) and sequence (ch28).
Cause -아서/어서, 때문에 — the first reason-giving beyond A1.
Purpose -기 위해서, duration 동안 — pairs with cause.
Contrast -지만/-는데도 — the counterweight to cause and purpose.
-(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 guessing: softens opinions, needs modifiers from ch21.
-기로 했어요/-게 됐어요 decisions: past tense in a fixed frame.
Particle expansion 에게/한테/께, 밖에 — a sweep once the core particles are solid.
이다 deep dive N이었어요/N인데 — needs past tense and -는데.
Family + N께서 V-(으)시- — the on-ramp to B1 honorifics.
Speech levels: sets the register frame the whole B1 band speaks in.
Honorifics -(으)시- — continues directly from 께서 in the previous chapter.
Discourse markers -는데/잖아요/죠/거든요 — the single biggest conversation win.
Social customs: applies 잖아요/거든요/는데요 the moment they are learned.
Opinions -는 것 같다 — same family as the discourse markers.
Housing: a topic chapter that only needs A1/A2 grammar — breathing room.
Reported speech -다고 했어요: requires past tense, which now precedes it.
-다고 하다/-냐고 하다 — the direct extension of reported speech.
Entertainment: uses -다고 했어요 from the two chapters before it.
Work and money -기로 하다/-(으)ㄹ까 봐/-게 되다.
Education: applies -기로 했어요 and -기 위해서 in a domain.
Feelings -는 척하다/-나 보다 — inference, after guessing is established.
Health: needs -아/어야 해요 and cause forms already covered.
-더라고요/-더니 retrospection: reporting your own past observation.
-길래/-는 바람에/-(으)ㄹ수록 — complex connectors, after -더니 in ch36.
Weather: uses -(으)ㄹ 텐데 and guessing forms.
Hedging -(으)ㄹ걸요/-겠-/-다면 — the fine control layer.
Clothing: -아/어 보이다 and comparisons in a domain.
-(으)ㄹ 수밖에 없다/-(으)ㄹ 리가 없다 — strong stance-taking.
Food culture: consolidation, grammar mostly already known.
Transport in depth: -(으)려고 해요 plus earlier direction forms.
Stacked modifiers and passive — the hardest B1 syntax, so it goes last.
은/는 vs 이/가 revisited — the B2 band opens by re-cutting the oldest particle.
-겠- volition and inference across registers.
-네요/-군요 attitude endings — speaker stance.
Nominalisation 기 vs 는 것: turns clauses into nouns.
Causatives -이/히/리/기 and -게 하다 — needs nominalisation to describe.
Unreal conditionals -았/었더라면: the most layered tense stacking.
Internet language: register awareness once every register is known.
Passive -이/히/리/기: needs the causative chapter to contrast against, and feeds the news register later.
Contracted reported speech -대요/-래요/-냬요/-재요: only lands once the full -다고 하다 forms are solid.
-느라고/-는 바람에/-더니/-았더니: reason connectors that need every earlier tense and subject rule in place.
-아/어 버리다/-고 말다/-(으)ㄹ 뻔하다/-(으)ㄴ 척하다: auxiliary endings that close the B2 band.
Advanced written Korean — the written register, separate from everything spoken.
Written connective endings and nominal -(으)ㅁ: the clause-internal layer under chapter-63's sentence connectors.
News and notice reading: needs the passive from chapter-66 and the written register from chapter-70.
Idioms and proverbs: the expressive layer, last before the closing synthesis review.
Synthesis and production review: the closing check over the whole course.
